title_seen: Planaria: Dynamic Architecture Fission for Spatial Multi-Tenant Acceleration of Deep Neural Networks
work_done: Proposes a 128x128 systolic accelerator built from omni-directional 32x32 subarrays that can be fissioned at run time into up to 16 logical accelerators to co-locate several DNN inference tasks; the compiler precompiles every fission configuration.
advantages: Fission plus a task scheduler gives 7.4x/7.2x/12.2x higher throughput than time-multiplexed PREMA at equal compute, memory and frequency for soft/medium/hard QoS; cycle counts from its simulator are checked against Verilog.
disadvantages: Targets multi-tenant datacenter inference; evaluated with a cycle-accurate simulator and 45 nm (FreePDK) synthesis of added logic, no silicon or FPGA; no number given for simulator-vs-Verilog agreement in the sections read.
relevance: Closest prior work for sub-array fission of a systolic array with compile-time-known per-configuration tiles/cycles; contrast: V3 splits one array per layer for latency, exact model = board.
read_locator: full text: abstract, Sec. III-IV (fission, compilation), Sec. VI-A methodology, area/power overhead paragraph
notes: Author PDF of the MICRO 2020 paper.

title_seen: FEATHER: A Reconfigurable Accelerator with Data Reordering Support for Low-Cost On-Chip Dataflow Switching
work_done: Presents FEATHER, a spatial array (NEST) with a multi-stage reduction network (BIRRD) that reorders data layout during reduction so dataflow and layout can switch per layer; adds layout modelling to Timeloop (Layoutloop) and deploys the design end to end on a ZCU104 FPGA.
advantages: Reports 1.27-2.89x latency speedup and 1.3-6.43x energy-efficiency gain over NVDLA, SIGMA and Eyeriss in Layoutloop, 2.65x/3.91x higher normalized throughput than Xilinx DPU/Gemmini on FPGA, at 6% area over a fixed-dataflow Eyeriss-like design.
disadvantages: Per-layer choice comes from a Layoutloop (Timeloop-based) EDP search, not validated against the board in the sections read; FPGA deployment of ResNet-50 uses only two layouts; DPU is faster on deep high-C/M layers (controller not optimized).
relevance: Closest flexible-dataflow FPGA design on a Zynq UltraScale+ board with a DPU baseline and DW layout; contrast for per-layer mode selection and latency reporting.
read_locator: full text: abstract, Sec. V (Layoutloop), Sec. VI-A setup, Sec. VI-B real-device latency (Fig. 12)
notes: arXiv version of ISCA 2024 paper; Crossref title truncated in listing but matches.

title_seen: Eyeriss v2: A Flexible Accelerator for Emerging Deep Neural Networks on Mobile Devices
work_done: Presents Eyeriss v2, a 192-PE row-stationary accelerator for compact and sparse DNNs with a hierarchical mesh NoC that adapts bandwidth and reuse per data type; a per-layer configuration command reconfigures the chip between layers, and PEs process compressed (CSC) sparse data.
advantages: With sparse MobileNet in 65 nm it reaches 1470.6 inferences/s and 2560.3 inferences/J at batch 1, 12.6x faster and 2.5x more energy efficient than Eyeriss v1 running MobileNet; the NoC handles depthwise and pointwise layers with low reuse.
disadvantages: Results are post-layout cycle-accurate gate-level simulations in 65 nm, not measured silicon; only one layer is processed at a time; the large MobileNet model was not benchmarked because post-layout simulation was too slow.
relevance: Key prior work on flexible on-chip networks for layer-shape variation (DW/PW) with per-layer reconfiguration; contrast to V3's fixed systolic links with per-layer modes.
read_locator: full text: abstract, Sec. I-III, Sec. V implementation results (Table IV)

title_seen: MAERI: Enabling Flexible Dataflow Mapping over DNN Accelerators via Reconfigurable Interconnects
work_done: Proposes MAERI, a DNN accelerator built from multiplier and adder switches connected by a configurable distribution tree and an augmented reduction tree, so arbitrary dataflows and layer partitions map by configuring small switches; implemented in Bluespec and synthesized in 28 nm at 200 MHz.
advantages: Reports 8-459% better utilization across dataflow mappings than rigid-NoC baselines and a 72.4% average speedup with about 95% multiplier utilization over a systolic array and an Eyeriss-like design with 64 MACs on AlexNet/VGG conv layers.
disadvantages: Synthesis tools report higher power than Eyeriss at equal compute; large filters (AlexNet 11x11, 5x5) lead to underutilization; ASIC synthesis plus simulation only.
relevance: Classic flexible-interconnect accelerator (reconfigurable reduction tree); contrast to V3's systolic array where flexibility is limited to per-layer modes.
read_locator: full text: abstract, Sec. 5 implementation, Sec. 6.1 evaluation
notes: Author-group PDF; already in docs/refs.bib as kwon2018maeri.

title_seen: SIGMA: A Sparse and Irregular GEMM Accelerator with Flexible Interconnects for DNN Training
work_done: Proposes SIGMA, a GEMM accelerator with flexible distribution and a Forwarding Adder Network (FAN) reduction tree that keeps PEs utilized for irregular GEMM shapes and arbitrary sparsity, targeting DNN training.
advantages: Reports 5.7x better performance than systolic arrays on irregular sparse matrices and about 3x over sparse accelerators; an instance reaches 10.8 TFLOPS efficiency at 65.10 mm^2 and 22.33 W in 28 nm.
disadvantages: Targets training-scale GEMMs in an ASIC (28 nm); flexibility comes from large distribution/reduction networks rather than a plain systolic array.
relevance: Motivates handling irregular (small/skinny) GEMM shapes that underuse systolic arrays, the case V3 addresses with split-K; contrast in hardware cost.
notes: No open full text found (OpenAlex: closed). Sparsity is part of SIGMA; placed here for its flexible interconnect, check overlap with cat 3.

title_seen: FlexFlow: A Flexible Dataflow Accelerator Architecture for Convolutional Neural Networks
work_done: Proposes FlexFlow, a CNN accelerator whose dataflow combines feature-map, neuron and synapse parallelism to reduce the mismatch between the parallelism a compute engine supports and the parallelism each CNN workload offers.
advantages: On six workloads it reports 2-10x speedup and 2.5-10x power-efficiency improvement over three accelerator architectures, and scales well with compute-engine size.
disadvantages: Only the abstract was read; evaluation scope (technology, simulation vs silicon) not checked.
relevance: Early flexible-dataflow CNN accelerator addressing per-layer parallelism mismatch, the same utilization problem V3 tackles with per-layer modes.
notes: Abstract withheld by Semantic Scholar; OpenAlex inverted-index abstract used. No open full text found.

title_seen: Self adaptive reconfigurable arrays (SARA): learning flexible GEMM accelerator configurations and mappings
work_done: Proposes a reconfigurable systolic array (RSA) that can act as one monolithic array or many smaller arrays of various aspect ratios with OS/WS/IS modes, and ADAPTNET, an ML recommender (with a hardware core, ADAPTNETX) that picks configuration and mapping per GEMM without search; SAGAR is a 32.768 TOPS instance.
advantages: ADAPTNET reaches 95% test accuracy against exhaustive search; SAGAR gives distributed-system mapping flexibility with 3.5x better power efficiency and 3.2x higher compute density.
disadvantages: Recommender labels come from SCALE-Sim runs; evaluated by architectural and post-layout simulation (28 nm), no board/silicon; a learned recommender can mispredict (95%).
relevance: Per-layer sub-array shape plus OS/WS/IS selection on a systolic array; contrast: V3 chooses modes with an exact cycle model at compile time.
read_locator: full text: abstract, Sec. III-IV (RSA, dataflow modes), SCALE-Sim labelling
notes: arXiv title differs: 'Learning Flexible GEMM Accelerator Configuration and Mapping-space using ML'; Crossref title of DAC 2022 version verified.

title_seen: Heterogeneous Dataflow Accelerators for Multi-DNN Workloads
work_done: Proposes heterogeneous dataflow accelerators (HDAs) that place several fixed-dataflow sub-accelerators on one chip, and Herald, a framework that co-optimizes hardware partitioning and layer scheduling using a MAESTRO-based cost model.
advantages: The identified HDA (Maelstrom) gives 65.3% lower latency and 5.0% lower energy than the best fixed-dataflow accelerator, and 22.0% lower energy at 20.7% higher latency than a reconfigurable accelerator.
disadvantages: Results come from the MAESTRO analytical cost model, not RTL or hardware measurement; targets multi-DNN AR/VR and MLPerf workloads.
relevance: Alternative to per-layer reconfiguration (layer-to-dataflow assignment at compile time); contrast for V3's single array with per-layer modes.
read_locator: full text: abstract, Sec. IV cost model (MAESTRO)

title_seen: Stream-K: Work-centric Parallel Decomposition for Dense Matrix-Matrix Multiplication on the GPU
work_done: Introduces Stream-K, a GEMM decomposition that gives each GPU core an even share of the aggregate inner-loop (K) iterations, with a fixup step that combines partial sums of tiles split across cores; also describes fixed-split (split-K) decomposition.
advantages: Peak speedups up to 14x and 6.7x and higher, more consistent average performance than CUTLASS and cuBLAS over 32,824 GEMM shapes, using one tile configuration per precision.
disadvantages: GPU software only (not a hardware accelerator); partial-sum fixup adds overhead that grows with finer splits.
relevance: Reference for reduction-dimension (split-K) partitioning to fix utilization on small output tiles; V3 applies split-K in an OS array, so split-K itself is not novel.
read_locator: full text: abstract, Sec. 1, Sec. 3.3 fixed-split, Sec. 4 Stream-K

title_seen: ArrayFlex: A Systolic Array Architecture with Configurable Transparent Pipelining
work_done: Proposes ArrayFlex, a weight-stationary systolic array whose pipeline can be set per CNN layer to normal or shallow depth by bypassing registers, trading cycles against clock frequency; implemented in SystemVerilog with a 28 nm library.
advantages: Selecting the pipeline configuration per layer reduces inference latency by 11% on average versus a fixed-pipeline array while using 13-23% less power, an EDP gain of 1.4-1.8x.
disadvantages: Needs a different clock frequency per pipeline mode (e.g. 2 GHz vs 1.7 GHz in 28 nm ASIC); evaluated by ASIC implementation and simulation, not on FPGA.
relevance: Per-layer configuration of a systolic array chosen analytically; contrast: V3 keeps one clock and changes only the mapping mode.
read_locator: full text: abstract, Sec. I, Sec. IV evaluation

title_seen: Gemmini: Enabling Systematic Deep-Learning Architecture Evaluation via Full-Stack Integration
work_done: Presents Gemmini, an open-source generator of systolic or vector DNN accelerators integrated in a RISC-V SoC with a software stack; PEs support weight- or output-stationary dataflow configurable at design time and run time; evaluated with FireSim cycle-exact simulation.
advantages: Captures system-level effects (OS, virtual memory, resource contention); generated accelerators were fabricated in TSMC 16 nm and Intel 22FFL and deliver up to three orders of magnitude speedup over CPUs.
disadvantages: Choice of dataflow per layer is left to the user/software; focuses on generator and SoC integration rather than a per-layer mode-selection model.
relevance: Run-time OS/WS switching in a systolic array with RTL-level (FireSim) evaluation; reference for OS/WS dual-mode arrays.
read_locator: full text: abstract, Sec. I-III (generator, dataflow)
